note: Synthetic data is generated from seeds at run time. FMA metadata (CC BY 4.0) was adopted on 2026-11-24 on the owner's approval (second round, 'Approve all'): it calibrates the synthetic catalogue and provides the EXP-004 real catalogue; listening stays simulated. Raw and processed FMA files are git-ignored and rebuilt by script. Licence statements were read on 2026-11-24 from the URLs given.

synthetic.generator: src/echo/catalogue.py (echo 0.1.0), parameters per run in each result file's config
synthetic.parameters: research/protocol.md section 3, with K, cluster weights and Zipf s calibrated on FMA (section 10.1)

candidates.license: Core data CC0; supplementary data CC BY-NC-SA 3.0
candidates.decision: Not needed for the current protocol; not downloaded

real.name: FMA: A Dataset For Music Analysis, fma_metadata.zip
real.citation: Defferrard, Benzi, Vandergheynst, Bresson. FMA: A Dataset For Music Analysis. ISMIR 2017. arXiv:1612.01840
real.licence: CC BY 4.0 for the metadata. README text read 2026-11-24: 'The metadata is released under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License (CC BY 4.0).' Also: 'The dataset is meant for research purposes.' Code MIT; audio under per-artist licences and never downloaded.
real.licence_checked: 2026-11-24; matches the owner's approval (owner-approvals-2026-11-24b.md section 1: 'FMA metadata, CC BY 4.0')
real.attribution: Derived values credit FMA (Defferrard et al.) under CC BY 4.0; changes: aggregation, standardisation, PCA, L2 normalisation.
real.commit_rule: Redistributable (CC BY 4.0) but 342 MiB, above the owner's 20 MB limit: data/raw/ is git-ignored
real.personal_data: No listener data. Artist and title fields exist in tracks.csv but are never read into the processed data.

calibration.content: aggregate values and counts only, no rows

catalogue.tolerance: byte-identical on rebuild on the freeze machine; other BLAS builds may differ in the last bits of the PCA, which changes the SHA-256 and makes EXP-004 refuse to run (fail closed)

uses: calibration of K, cluster weights and Zipf s (training split)
